name: Hospitals (operations and admin)

problems.words: Discharge takes six hours because the bill isn't ready
quick_ideas: Time-stamp each clearance step on a few discharges, so the slowest step is visible
Start bill preparation when the discharge decision is made, so billing isn't the last thing to begin.

workzap_build.text: a discharge tracker showing every clearance step with time stamps and which role is holding it, on every ward, with daily average discharge time and no patient details beyond a reference.

problems.ask_first: Which step usually takes longest, the insurer or internal returns?
problems.free_stops: The step list, escalation rules and who sees what are laid out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note when files reach billing and when bills are ready for a few discharges, so you see the real billing wait.
Hand one admin role the daily list of expected discharges before noon, so billing can prepare earlier the same day.

problems.words: Beds are empty on paper but full in reality, nobody updates the board
quick_ideas: Do one ward walk-round comparing the board with reality, so you know how far off it is
Agree a few simple bed statuses everyone uses, so updates mean the same thing.

workzap_build.text: dashboards_reports — a bed board on screen and phone updated by ward and housekeeping roles, showing each bed's status by ward in real time with no patient names.

problems.ask_first: Does your HIS have a bed module staff could use?
problems.free_stops: Status definitions and who updates when are set in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare one shift's bed board updates with a walk round of rooms, so you see which ward misses updates most.
Make the charge nurse role update the bed board at one fixed handover time, so the next team starts from the same picture.

problems.words: Insurance rejections are eating our month
quick_ideas: List this month's rejections by reference and reason, so the top paperwork gap shows up
Give each rejected claim a resubmission date, so none are forgotten.

workzap_build.text: dashboards_reports — an insurance, panel and health-card receivables tracker with claim ageing, rejection reasons and resubmission dates, summarised by payer every day.

problems.ask_first: Are government health-card claims handled by the same team?
problems.free_stops: The status flow and payer reports are detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Sort this month's rejections by reason on paper and mark repeats, so the paperwork error hurting claims stands out.
Give one billing role a fixed daily slot to chase rejected claims from one notebook, so resubmissions stop drifting.

problems.words: Patients leave without clearing the final bill
quick_ideas: Share a running estimate with attendants midway through a stay, so the final bill isn't a surprise
List open balances by reference, so follow-up starts within days.

workzap_build.text: customer_messaging — a running account per admission reference with advance, charges and balance, and bill updates sent only to the registered contact with their permission.

problems.ask_first: Do you take an advance at admission for cash patients?
problems.free_stops: When estimates go out and how balances are chased is set in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many final bills stayed unpaid this week and note where discharge papers were at the time, so the hold-up is clearer.
Give one front desk role the job of checking open balances before discharge papers leave admin, so fewer accounts slip past settlement.

problems.words: Wards indent the same item twice and the store issues both
quick_ideas: Check one week of indents for repeats, so you see how often it happens
Ask wards to sign for each issue, so receipt is confirmed.

workzap_build.text: a ward indent and store system with approval, issue and receipt confirmation that flags repeat indents and items sent but not received, with ward-wise consumption reports.

problems.ask_first: Does each ward keep its own stock cupboard?
problems.free_stops: The approval chain and flag rules are designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Mark repeated item requests from the same ward over one week, so you see which supplies are being indented twice.
Keep one indent notebook in the store and make one store role check repeat requests before issuing, so duplicate issues reduce.

problems.words: Pharmacy stock expires on the shelf while we buy more of it
quick_ideas: Pull one near-expiry list from the pharmacy, so purchasing sees it before ordering
Check other stores for the same item before buying, so stock moves first.

workzap_build.text: transfer_tracking — an expiry register that sends near-expiry alerts and suggests transfers between stores before new orders, across all sites.

problems.ask_first: Is the pharmacy run in-house or outsourced?
problems.free_stops: Alert timing and transfer rules stay for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk one pharmacy shelf and note items expiring soon that were also bought recently, so buying and stock movement can be compared.
Give one pharmacy role a fixed weekly near expiry review with purchasing notes in one notebook, so older stock gets attention before reordering.

problems.words: Purchase approvals sit with the MD for days
quick_ideas: List what is waiting and for how long, so the delay is visible
Agree which small purchases don't need the MD, so the queue shrinks.

workzap_build.text: a purchase request and approval chain on WhatsApp with limits per role, automatic reminders and a log of who approved what and when.

problems.ask_first: Do requests wait for quotes or simply for the MD's time?
problems.free_stops: The approval limits and reminder flow are set in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count purchase requests waiting with the MD today and note their oldest waiting time, so the approval pile has a clear size.
Set one daily handover time when one admin role places all pending approvals together for the MD, so requests stop arriving piecemeal.

problems.words: Nursing roster is made on paper and changes every day
quick_ideas: Publish next week's roster in one shared place, so everyone works from the same version
Record agency hours daily, so the agency invoice can be checked.

workzap_build.text: cash_reconciliation — a roster with swaps and leave handled by the supervisor role, and agency hours checked against agency invoices every month.

problems.ask_first: How many of your nurses come through agencies?
problems.free_stops: Swap rules and the invoice check are detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare this week's planned roster with actual duty changes on paper, so you see which shift changes most often.
Keep one roster copy in one agreed place and make one nursing admin role mark every change there, so staff stop following different versions.

problems.words: Equipment breaks and nobody knows when it was last serviced
quick_ideas: List major equipment with last service date and vendor contact, so gaps are visible
Send all breakdown reports to one number, so the biomedical team hears first.

workzap_build.text: a biomedical asset register with service-due reminders, breakdown reports, downtime tracking and vendor response times.

problems.ask_first: Is maintenance in-house or with vendors?
problems.free_stops: The register fields and reminder schedule are set in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk through major equipment and note which items have no visible last service record, so the biggest record gaps stand out.
Give one biomedical role one notebook for service dates and breakdown handovers, so maintenance history stops getting split across departments.

problems.words: Every department has its own Excel and none of them agree
quick_ideas: Agree a short list of monthly numbers each department sends, so everyone reports the same things
Name one owner per number, so disputes have one answer.

workzap_build.text: integration — a management dashboard with admissions, occupancy, revenue by payer and department and receivables, with HIS billing connected to accounts so totals agree daily.

problems.ask_first: Which number do you most need earlier?
problems.free_stops: Data sources and connections are mapped in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare last month's admissions total from each department's sheet for one day, so you see which source disagrees most often.
Keep one notebook page for number disputes and assign one admin role to close each mismatch, so arguments stop circling between departments.

problems.words: Complaints get lost between the ward, admin and the MD's office
quick_ideas: Put this month's open complaints in one list with an owner role, so each has someone responsible
Review that list once with the MD, so stuck ones are seen.

workzap_build.text: a complaint log with owner role, deadline, reminders and closure notes, visible to the MD, with no patient health details recorded.

problems.ask_first: Who is meant to close a complaint today?
problems.free_stops: Deadlines and escalation steps are set in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count open complaints sitting in the ward, admin and the MD office today, so you see where handovers are failing.
Give one admin role the job of updating a single complaints notebook at a fixed daily time, so nothing stalls between offices.

never_say: Any view on clinical care, staffing ratios as a safety matter, infection control or whether a complication was avoidable.
Suggestions to inflate bills, add services not given, alter claim codes or change discharge dates.
Interpretations of PHC, DHA, DOH, MOHAP or accreditation standards.
Legal advice on complaints threatening legal action; point to the hospital's lawyer.
Ideas that link a bed or room to a named patient, or put health information in messages.
Promises that discharge will take a set number of hours.

sample_reply.person: Discharge is our biggest headache. Patient is ready by 11 but the family is still sitting at 5 waiting for the bill. What can we do?
sample_reply.pi: Yes, this can be improved, and you can start this week. 1) Time-stamp each clearance step on a few discharges, so you can see exactly where the hours go. 2) Start the bill when the discharge decision is made, so billing isn't the last thing to begin. Workzap can do this automatically for you with a discharge tracker that shows every step and which role is holding it, measured daily on every ward and without patient details on screen. Shall I have a solution document and quote prepared for you? You're welcome to say no.
